name: jumpnbump
title: Jump 'n Bump (Brainchild Design, 1998 — DOS/DJGPP)
fetch: git clone https://gitlab.com/LibreGames/jumpnbump.git corpus/jumpnbump && mkdir -p corpus/jumpnbump-dos && git -C corpus/jumpnbump archive $(git -C corpus/jumpnbump rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD) | tar -x -C corpus/jumpnbump-dos
_doc: THE ORIGINAL DOS SOURCE, and getting to it took some archaeology worth recording. The obvious trees are ports: the project's current head is SDL2, tag 1.51 is SDL 1.2, and even tag 0.72 -- which still carries dos/ -- CANNOT build for DOS, because its config.h opens with `#undef DOS` and every unit includes it through globals.h. A -DDOS on the command line is cancelled before it is read, so a DOS build there would mean EDITING the source. The one tree that is DOS without being selected is the CVS import at the repository's ROOT COMMIT (13 Feb 2002, 'Initial revision'): no config.h, no sdl/, no platform guard anywhere -- globals.h includes conio.h, dpmi.h, sys/nearptr.h, pc.h and dj.h unconditionally. Nothing to choose and nothing to patch. Brainchild's own tarball is not recoverable: brainchilddesign.com serves an empty page today, and the Wayback Machine has jnb-src.zip only as a 404 from 2021 -- the period download page offers the game and no source at all.
_units: modify/pack.c and modify/unpack.c are separate TOOLS that build the .dat file, not part of the game, and each has its own main().
_include: dj.h sits in dos/ and globals.h asks for it as <dj.h>, so dos/ is on the include path rather than the header being moved.
_sound: dj is a LIBRARY, and it ships here as dos/libdj.a with no source -- the binary names its own six units (dj.c mixer.c mod.c sb.c sb_dma.c sfx.c), a Sound Blaster DMA mixer with MOD playback. That is the Allegro and SEAL situation exactly (P1.7): the library is shimmed from its header, never compiled. dj.h declares 40 functions. NOTE that silence is not a compile-time option here -- NOSOUND exists in the later ports' config.h and is tested nowhere in the code -- but the API itself offers dj_set_nosound, which the program calls, so a silent build uses the library's own switch rather than an invented one.
_asm: dos/gfx.S is NASM syntax despite the .S extension ([GLOBAL _x], [SECTION .text]), and exports exactly TWO symbols: get_block and put_block, over ___djgpp_base_address. gfx.c does carry C versions of both, but inside #if 0 -- so they are not a build option the program offers, and enabling them would be editing the source. This is the first target in the corpus where assembly is NOT sidesteppable, which is a real data point for P5.2: that row measured an assembler buys ONE symbol corpus-wide, because every other game ships C twins its own build can select.
